p:cNvPr.descr: Colored graph with bars divided according to the lipid composition of rat hepatocyte membranes. A graph shows the lipid composition of various membranes in rat liver cells. The graph’s vertical axis is labeled “rat hepatocyte membrane type.” There are no values on the axis; instead the types of membranes are listed along the axis. From the top, they are: plasma, inner mitochondrial, outer mitochondrial, lysosomal, nuclear, rough ER, smooth ER, and Golgi. The horizontal axis is labeled “percent membrane lipid” with range 0 to 100 and interval 20. At the bottom there is a key with colored squares labeled with the lipids they represent. From the top left, orange represents cholesterol, red represents cardiolipin, pale yellow represents minor lipids, green represents sphingolipids, light blue represents phosphatidylcholine, dark blue represents phosphatidylethanolamine. The bars go all the way across the graph and are colored according to their percent composition. For plasma, cholesterol reaches to 40%, phosphatidylcholine reaches 40 to 58%, phosphatidylethanolamine reaches from 58 to 70%, minor lipids reaches from 70 to 80%, and sphingolipids reach from 80 to 100%. Below, inner mitochondrial membrane, cholesterol reaches from 0 to 5%, cardiolipin from 5 to 20%, phosphatidylcholine from 20% to 70%, phosphatidylethanolamine from 70% to 84%, minor lipids from 84 to 92%, and sphingolipids from 92 to 100%. Below, the outer mitochondrial membrane consists of cholesterol from 0 to 10%, cardiolipin from 10 to 15%, phosphatidylcholine from 15 to 60%, phosphatidylethanolamine from 60 to 85%, minor lipids from 85 to 95%, and sphingolipids from 95% to 100%. Below, the lysosomal membrane has cholesterol from 0 to 15%, cardiolipin from 15 to 21%, phosphatidylcholine from 21% to 50%, phosphatidylethanolamine from 50 to 65%, minor lipids from 65 to 70%, and sphingolipids from 70 to 100%. Below this, the nuclear membrane has cholesterol from 0 to 15%, phosphatidylcholine from 15 to 70%, phosphatidylethanolamine from 70 to 85%, minor lipids from 85 to 95%, and sphingolipids from 95 to 100%. Below, rough ER has cholesterol from 0 to 10%, phosphatidylcholine from 10 to 65%, phosphatidylethanolamine from 65 to 85%, minor lipids from 85 to 95%, and sphingolipids from 95 to 100%. Below this, smooth ER has cholesterol 0 to 15%, cardiolipin from 15 to 17%, phosphatidylcholine from 17 to 60%, phosphatidylethanolamine from 60 to 80%, minor lipids from 80 to 85%, and sphingolipids from 90 to 100%. Finally, the Golgi has cholesterol from 0 to 10%, phosphatidylcholine from 10 to 55%, phosphatidylethanolamine from 55 to 75%, minor lipids from 75 to 90%, and sphingolipids from 90 to 100%.
